story: At 8:17 on a humid, hazy Saturday morning in Sumter Oaks, Gary is bench-testing speaker wiring at his workbench, keeping everything indoors and off the golf cart. Donna is at her house checking the club calendar, where she has court one with Gary and a cobbler on the books for Rosa at five. Hal is out with his binoculars on a slow sweep of Magnolia Loop, making sure the flamingos stay behind the hedge and the carts are parked right, while Rosa, feeling hopeful, starts prepping the main dish for tonight's welcome dinner in her kitchen.
events: Gary (gary workbench): Bench-test the speaker wiring indoors, nothing mounted to the cart
Donna (donna club calendar): Check today's schedule: court one with Gary, cobbler for Rosa's at five
Hal (hal binoculars): Do a slow morning sweep of Magnolia Loop to confirm flamingos stay behind the hedge and carts are parked right
Rosa (rosa kitchen): Start prepping the main dish for tonight's welcome dinner

gary.thought_process: It's Saturday morning, and the review application is filed but not approved, so nothing gets mounted to the cart yet. Quiet hours are over at 7, but I've been bench-testing indoors and nothing needs to go on the street. I can keep tinkering at the workbench on the sound system side, staying inside the house, and keep busy until the afternoon pickleball with Donna and dinner at Rosa's at five.

parameters.content: Bench-test the speaker wiring indoors, nothing mounted to the cart

donna.thought_process: It's Saturday morning, and I'm home alone with a full day ahead: court one with Gary this afternoon, then the cobbler and ice cream for Rosa's at five. Before I load up the cart, I should check the club calendar so I don't double-book anything and remember the two-hour court limit. Nobody's around to talk to, so a quick check of the schedule is the most useful thing to do right now.

parameters.content: Check today's schedule: court one with Gary, cobbler for Rosa's at five

hal.thought_process: The notebook says nothing is pending. Gary's paperwork is filed, Donna's flamingos are behind the hedge, and the street is quiet. Dinner at Rosa's is Saturday evening and I've already written down the reminder: cornbread, table, on time. It's only 8 AM, so there's no sense rushing off. I've already sat on the porch and reviewed the notebook, so no sense repeating that. Best use of the morning is to get the binoculars and do my usual sweep of Magnolia Loop, quietly making sure everything is still in order before I turn my attention to the cornbread.

parameters.content: Do a slow morning sweep of Magnolia Loop to confirm flamingos stay behind the hedge and carts are parked right

rosa.thought_process: It's Saturday morning, dinner is at five, and I'm alone at home. The long table is already set with the cloth and the seating is planned. Hal has the cornbread, Donna the cobbler, Gary the ice and chairs, so the only piece left on my plate is my own cooking. I haven't done much with the kitchen yet, so I should get started on the main dish now, since it will take hours and I still want time to rest before the neighbors arrive. I also have a per-diem shift schedule to glance at, but the dinner is the priority today.

parameters.content: Start prepping the main dish for tonight's welcome dinner

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
